To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a robust segmentation component can be built by combining a finite state morpheme analyzer with a text normalization component, (b) a broad coverage Japanese parser can be constructed by adding a finite state morphemic analyzer, a text normalizer and a finite state lattice generator to an existing parser, and (c) by combining these two components, we have built a robust, broad coverage Japanese parser that achieves a breaking accuracy in excess of 97% over a variety of corpora.

a) a finite state segmentation approach is well suited for Japanese, where the task is complicated by orthographic variation, and b) a lattice of word segmentation candidates can be used effectively to improve the performance of a Japanese NL parser.

(1) a lattice representation of word candidates can be produced by a morphological analyzer with a high recall, (2) a lattice representation is useful for parsing, and (3) a lattice representation allows a broad coverage parser to achieve a high breaking accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of robust and flexible text analysis components that can be used as the basis of a broad coverage NL system.
the following question: how much linguistic knowledge can we afford to leave out of the segmentation process in order to achieve the best possible performance on a broad coverage parser?
the design of robust segmentation algorithms that are capable of handling the complex orthographic variation found in Japanese text.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the parser is a good parser, and the segmenter is a good segmenter.
the parser is able to achieve high precision and recall on the test set, but the segmentation accuracy is low.
the parser is robust and accurate, and the segmenter is fast and accurate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a robust, high performance Japanese word segmentation system that is suitable for use as a component of a broad coverage Japanese natural language processing system.
the parser can be made more robust by allowing the segmenter to produce a large number of candidate analyses.
we have designed a system that can handle the orthography of Japanese, and that can be integrated with a broad coverage parser to yield a high degree of accuracy in word segmentation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple finite-state segmenter that is designed to maximize recall and minimize the number of false positives can provide a robust lattice of segmentation candidates for a broad-coverage NL parser.
the use of a lattice of segmentation hypotheses can greatly increase the robustness of the parser without a significant increase in the amount of linguistic knowledge required.
it is possible to build a robust, general-purpose Japanese segmenter that can handle a wide range of orthographic variation without requiring a large amount of linguistic knowledge.
